findings.message: Criterion 6's first bullet asks for a test showing the engine-verb decision is true for `drain`/`serve` and false for `triage`, `eval` and a missing `verb` key. `test_engine_verbs` never calls production code. It re-evaluates its own copy, `holder.get("verb") in ENGINE_VERBS`, so it only pins which verbs the constant contains. The real decision in `_require_engine` (`(exc.holder or {}).get("verb") or "unknown holder"`, then the membership test) is never run for `drain`, `eval`, a missing key or a `None` holder. A regression there, such as a changed fallback or an inverted check, would not fail this test.
findings.paved_road: Drive the real path for each case. Extend `test_request_routing` (or a new parametrized test) so the holder covers `drain`, `serve`, `triage`, `eval`, a dict without `verb`, and `None`, each raising `LockHeld` from the fake `Lockfile.acquire`. Assert that `_control`/`_verdict`/`_retro` publish exactly one request for `drain` and `serve`, and raise `runner.Refusal` and publish nothing for the other cases. Then delete the copied-expression test.
